output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses comes mainly from the 12 August move of the alarm relay server, not from agency staff or the nurses involved. The hardware move was reported as like-for-like. In fact, 11 of the 14 forwarding rules were silently skipped during import. Those rules held back brief SpO2 alerts, suppressed repeat notifications, and sent probe-off alarms to the charge phone only. Since then, phone notifications per nurse in Pods A-C have roughly doubled, and acknowledgement times have doubled. Pod D was still on the old server and shows no change. Core, agency and new-graduate nurses all show the same jump after 12 August. Agency share was similar in Pod D, which argues against a staffing explanation. Monitor alarm volume is flat, so acuity and the September monitor software update are not the cause. Sick leave probably rose partly from alarm fatigue, but a hospital-wide virus season is a competing explanation. How sure: high. Recommend rejecting the agency cap and the performance reviews. Restore the old forwarding rules with clinical validation and sign-off. Then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Look separately at the Room 14 phone complaints and at your relay change-testing process.
